name: fdivp
title: IEEE 754 division PARAMETRIC in the format (exponent width W, precision P, storage W+P bits), round to nearest even, for every W >= 2, P >= 2
_range_comment: Each range string states the bounds of Spec.lean's `inRange` that involve its parameter (2 <= W, 2 <= P, W + P + 1 < 2^31; the sum decided 2026-11-06): the port width W + P and the exponent width W + P + 1 a design computes in are int expressions of the module, and every such width stays in the 32-bit int range, where a real elaboration and ls-sv agree.

banlist._comment: The divider bans run-time division and remainder (the operator that IS the task); ** for safety. + - * and comparisons stay allowed.

_bv_decide_comment: The svGolf rules allow bv_decide on fixed-size subgoals in principle and this task is fixed-size, but bv_decide runs an external SAT solver (cadical) and the checker does not support external solvers (decided 2026-11-01), so check.py refuses allow_bv_decide: true (an infrastructure error); svgolf/README.md, 'bv_decide'. Proofs use propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

postsynth._comment: The corner lists are fixed hex strings for the 16-bit scoring point (5, 11), binary16 (a different scoring point needs its own lists): 18 x 18 special operand pairs (signed zeros, the extreme subnormals and normals, +-1, +-max, +-inf, NaNs), those of the former 16-bit task; with the harvested comparison constants and 4000 seeded random pairs.

references.note: the proved reference (WP-H3): D3, a word-level netlist of 34 sites for every W, P >= 2 (a linear one-bit normalizer and the P + 2 restoring steps as generate families, a two's complement exponent, a run-time shifter with a sticky bit, round to nearest even by an increment into {exponent, fraction}); sv_structure with a rank certificate, sv_interface, sv_equations (about 0.24 and 0.32 M heartbeats with the WP-LIN grouping), then ONE theorem, `Glue.chain` (section DpG5), from the 34 printed equations to the value of q, and OutN_fdivBits (section DpU) for the arithmetic; the file is self-contained over the general library LeanModels.Sv.Lib: the facts about the spec (section IEEE754Proofs), the rounding certificate (CertF), the math layer (DpN..DpU) and the glue (DpG1..DpG5) are its sections

the second proved reference (PLAN4 N1), a Newton-Raphson divider: D3 with its P + 2 restoring steps replaced by an initial reciprocal r0 = 45/32 - 15/32 d, NI = $clog2((P + 9) / 8) + 1 Newton steps r <- r (2 - d r) (a generate family over word-level `*`; the step count is logarithmic in P), a quotient estimate at most 2 below the quotient and an exact correction by the remainder modulo 2^(P+2); unpacking, normalizers, exponent, denormalizer, rounding and output stage are D3's. Not competitive (7892.452 GE, depth 252 at (5, 11), against D3's 2166.076, 289), a reference for a second algorithm. sv_structure with a rank certificate (0.32 M heartbeats; the whole solution 0.54 M), sv_interface, sv_equations, then its own `Glue.chain` (section NwG2) over the 46 printed equations, the core (section NwG1) on the reference's own section NwCore (`newton_rest`: the core's quotient and sticky are restoring division's); self-contained like D3, whose sections IEEE754Proofs..DpG4 it copies verbatim (tests/fdivp/shared_sections.py checks that they stay byte-identical)

the third proved reference (PLAN4, the SRT workflow), a radix-4 SRT divider adapted from CORE-V Wally (Apache-2.0 WITH SHL-2.1; the provenance header lists the ten changes, the licence texts are in reference/LICENSES/): D3 with its P + 2 restoring steps replaced by N = (P + 2) / 2 + 1 unrolled stages (a generate family `srt`), each selecting a digit in {-2, ..., 2} by comparing a 7-bit estimate of the carry-save remainder with four constants chosen by 3 divisor bits (3-level ?: trees over Wally's constants), one carry-save row 4 (R - q d) and on-the-fly conversion of the digits; then the correction by the residual's sign and the sticky rs != 0; unpacking, normalizers, exponent, denormalizer, rounding and output stage are D3's. The lowest depth of the three (2787.652 GE, depth 189 at (5, 11), against D3's 2166.076, 289). sv_structure with a rank certificate (19 ranks per stage) returning the shared obligations, sv_interface, sv_equations, then its own `Glue.chain` (section SrG2) over the 69 printed equations and the core (section SrG1) on the mathematics of section SrCore (`srt_rest`: after N stages the corrected quotient and sticky are restoring division's; the selection table checked cell by cell by one kernel `decide`); self-contained like D3, whose sections IEEE754Proofs..DpG4 it copies verbatim (tests/fdivp/shared_sections.py)

_time_limit_comment: ONE limit for every task, a ceiling (decided 2026-11-02): 300 CPU s since 2026-11-06, 120 s of wall clock when the runs below were made; a reference whose cold solution stage is over it is a defect of the proof to fix, not a limit to raise. In CPU seconds, what the limit counts (2026-11-06, three cold check.py --no-score runs each, score/time_limits.json): fdivp 82.2, 79.1 and 80.4, fdivp_newton 120.7, 108.3 and 108.4, fdivp_srt 181.8, 160.5 and 160.2 CPU s, fdivp_srt over the 150 CPU s target. The wall-clock runs below came first. Since 2026-11-03 the reference proof is self-contained (no proof library in the tasks library: the spec's facts, the certificate, the math layer and the glue are compiled in the solution stage; only LeanModels.Sv.Lib is prebuilt). Cold `solution` stage of the reference, three check.py runs (fresh --stage-dir each, one run at a time, each taking the Lean slot itself, LEAN_NUM_THREADS=2, nice 19; load average at the start 9.5, 6.0, 6.8 from other jobs): 70.3, 64.5, 71.6 s (leanchecker 39.4, 35.2, 44.6 s of its 900), above the 60 s target. Before the fold (the Dp* modules prebuilt in the tasks library, 2026-11-02, load 14, 11, 8): 31.0, 26.0, 24.8 s. The Newton reference (reference/fdivp_newton.lean, 2026-11-04, measured the same way, load average 5 to 6): 44.59, 45.80, 45.30 s (leanchecker 33.9, 34.0, 35.9 s). The SRT reference (reference/fdivp_srt.lean, 2026-11-05, measured the same way, each run started at a load average below 8: 7.7, 7.4, 6.7): 78.58, 73.19, 69.92 s (leanchecker 49.4, 47.6, 46.1 s), the slowest of the three; score/time_limits.json had that record until 2026-11-06.
